    }

  "exhaustiveness": 0.15,
  "rationale": "The technical claim requires the added columns to be constitutive facets (parts) of operational_burden, each an 'aspect OF' the concept realized as a separate, non-overlapping dimension. Instead, all three columns operate on a single flat taxonomy of burden categories: one packs every category into a multi-label field, one counts them, and one picks the primary one. None isolates a distinct constitutive aspect of the concept (e.g., a dedicated column per burden dimension such as service impact, resolution effort, recurrence, resource contention). The underlying category tokens are also not MECE among themselves: they conflate fault type, affected service, and symptom, so several can co-occur (connectivity_issue|server_outage|database_burden), violating mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is judged low because the schema captures only one axis (a type label) of the multi-dimensional notion of operational burden and omits effort, impact scope, and duration dimensions. The set is essentially a single multi-label classifier presented in three views, not a faceted decomposition, so it fails the test."
